wine: Sonoma Vineyards River West Old Vines Zinfandel (Estate Bottled)
fallback_tasting_notes: Historical / producer context: Rod Strong founded Sonoma Vineyards in 1959; renamed to Rodney Strong Vineyards in 1980 — so this 1977 bottling is from the original 'Sonoma Vineyards' era. River West Vineyard (Middle Reach of Russian River Valley) was first planted in the 1930s and contains 100-year-old Zinfandel vines; at the time of this bottling Strong was farming it under a long-term arrangement (official acquisition: 2023). Label legitimately uses 'Estate Bottled' designation because the winery controlled the vineyard operation even pre-ownership. Old-vine Russian River Zinfandel can age surprisingly well when stored properly; 1970s Zins from Ridge, Ravenswood, and similar old-vine sources have shown at 40+ years. 1977 was a solid (not legendary) California vintage. Subregion 'Russian River Valley' used here for geographic accuracy — the RRV AVA itself wasn't established until 1983, so the 1977 label likely just says 'Sonoma County'. No vintage-specific professional note located. At 49 years old, condition is everything — check fill, cork, and capsule before opening.

Whole-cluster pressed, ~30-day ferment in predominantly neutral oak, partial malolactic, batonnage. Fruit sourced from Toyon Farm (Carneros, Napa side). Final chemistry not published on 2024 tech sheet (2023 had full chem, Porter dropped it for 2024). 2024 growing season: heavy winter rains followed by 40+ days of intense summer heat; strong canopies preserved fruit quality, harvest back to typical timing after variable years.

fallback_tasting_notes: House style across vintages: Aonair's Mountains Proprietary is a Bordeaux-style blend from Napa's mountain AVAs — opaque ruby, dark-fruit aromatics (cassis, black cherry, blackberry, plum), plush, fruit-forward palate with moderate, well-integrated, gravelly tannins. Producer's style is 'approachable young but age-worthy,' explicitly avoiding the massive tannin structure common to mountain Napa Cabs. 2023 Napa was cool and late (widely called 'Vintage of a Lifetime') — expect brighter acidity, longer hang-time complexity, and more restrained ripeness than the 2021. No 2023-specific professional note located.

tasting_notes: Dave (The Napa Wine Project, 2023): "Highly aromatic — the aromatics fly out of the glass immediately upon pouring. Its scents are a union of both red and darker fruits including Santa Rosa plum, dark raspberries, ripe blackberry and boysenberry. Fully ripe but with flavor, acidity and texture in harmony, this wine tastes like Satsuma plum, boysenberry, blackberry and Persian mulberry. The savory and dark finish lingers with grainy and gravelly textured tannins ultimately pacing the fruit on the finish.". | Producer/house context: Grant Long Jr. sources from iron-rich rocky soils of the El Dorado Sierra foothills; oak used as 'an integrating tool rather than a dominating one,' crafted smooth and drinkable young yet structured for aging. The 2017 showed well-evolved tertiary aromas (dark pepper, dried herbs, sage, tobacco, old cedar, leather) with resolved tannins, suggesting a ~7-yr-plus aging arc. Specific 2023 blend components and tech specs (ABV/pH/barrel program/cases) not publicly located.

Then the power and stony intensity pour over you in a giant wave. The freshness is extraordinary for this hot and dry vintage. Serious tannins in the very long, compact and refined finish." | Jeb Dunnuck (96 pts): blend ~40% Mourvèdre, 30% Grenache, 10% Counoise, 10% Syrah, balance permitted varieties — darker, more serious and focused from the higher Mourvèdre component. | Wine Advocate: 94+.

impressions.note: First pour, out at a steak restaurant. Mourvèdre-forward meatiness paired great with the steak; bitter-almond finish blended in well after a ~30 min rest. Reputation well deserved.

tasting_notes: Chateau Musar (1997 vintage sheet): bright golden straw; almond, cashew, vanilla, buttery toast and honey; rich, warm and dry with herbs, spiced apple, fresh acidity and a long finish. Bartholomew Broadbent (2019): deep gold, dry-Sauternes-like depth, walnut and cognac-like complexity; continued opening through day three.
verdict: Fucking fabulous. A profoundly evolved, oxidative white that opened from mineral, herb and wood into baked apple, baking spice and honey while staying dry, high-acid and deeply persistent.

impressions.note: First glass: Looks and smells like a sweet dessert wine, but drinks dry, complex and mineral, with a looooong mineral hang. Primary fruit is essentially gone except as implied by the acidity; instead there’s a hard-to-disentangle melody of intertwined wood, mineral and herbs. Slight astringency is balanced by body, flavor depth and high acid, all wrapped in obvious oxidative character.
Glass 2, after some rest: apple emerged through the oxidative, mineral and herbal character.

Glass 3, the last glass: baking spices on the nose, and the whole wine loosened way up. Clear baked apple emerged on both nose and palate. The astringency backed down while the mineral and herbal character remained and unfurled further. Honey throughout, but only the slightest hint of sweetness. Nice one — big ups!

Surprisingly substantial body for a white, with a pleasurable phenolic bite; the nose remained restrained. Structurally compelling but recognizably white-wine complexity, less layered than the 2025 Acquiesce Grenache Blanc. Enjoyable, though not category-converting.

James Suckling (96 pts, 2019): vibrant red fruit and flowers, raspberry and red plum, spiced orange and yellow peach, linear tannin, power and focus. Vinous (Josh Raynolds, 94 pts, 2010): raspberry, cherry, blood orange, dried flowers, lavender, rose and pepper; balanced and pure. | Producer/house context: approximately 90% Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and Cinsault from very old vines; partially destemmed, fermented in concrete and stainless steel, then aged 12-14 months in concrete without oak.
verdict: Very well balanced and a good showcase for mature flavors, but not a show-stopper: it lacked the interest and concentration to be compelling beyond the meal.

impressions.note: With dinner: Thankfully not excessively volatile. Mature flavor profile, very well balanced, and worked well as a meal wine. Not especially interesting or concentrated beyond that; the Grenache-centric composition may explain some of that character.
